rv.q: At a cultural moment when empathy feels alarmingly scarce, Zack’s sweet humanity lands with unexpected force.
While Zack may not be among Brighouse's finest achievements, the play might benefit from an approach that delicately plumbs the covert charms
a delightful rediscovered comedy of character with many colorful roles which actors can sink their teeth into
Even when the loosey goosey narrative beats feel arbitrary, the writers at least keep it funny and light.
This time it’s plucked a British play written in 1916 by Harold Brighouse called Zack.

cn.t: The Mint Theater's revival of Brighouse's 1916 play divides critics. Some find it a charming Edwardian comedy, while others deem the production stale and inadequately staged, suggesting this forgotten work may have been better left undiscovered.
